answer: A sybil swarm is cheap only when identities are free, so each agent should lock a refundable stake and earn weight slowly. Picture a quartz-hard bond: a newcomer parks funds in a haven escrow, and its voting power grows only as peers verify real work. Splitting one budget across an orchard of fake accounts dilutes each stake, so forging a thousand identities costs a thousand bonds plus months of waiting, and slashing burns them on detected collusion.
